newsitem.title: INDONESIA: FOCUS-Indonesia inflation contained, surplus down.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Indonesia inflation contained, surplus down.

text.p: Indonesia's inflation slowed in May while the trade surplus fell significantly in March but officials said on Wednesday the economy was in good shape.
Economists said fundamentals remained sound, with the independent Pacific Economic Cooperation Council forecasting growth of 7.3 and 7.8 percent in 1997 and 1998 respectively.
Information Minister Harmoko said after a monthly cabinet meeting that inflation rose 0.19 percent month-on-month in May, compared with an increase of 0.56 percent in April.
Year-on-year inflation in May was 5.08 percent, compared with 4.95 percent in April, while the trade surplus fell to $243.3 million in March from $964.3 million in February.
Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita told Reuters the country's economy was in good shape, with prices under control while the economy was likely to grow more than seven percent.

"Our economy is in a good shape. Inflation in May has slowed down. I think inflation will be around five percent for this year," Ginanjar said, adding that the financial markets had withstood the violent general election campaign.
President Suharto's ruling Golkar party emerged victorious in last Thursday's election, gathering more than 74 percent of the votes. Nearly 125 million Indonesians were eligible to vote.

"Our economy is stable with lower inflation. The value of the rupiah is also stable," Harmoko told reporters after the monthly cabinet meeting chaired by Suharto. But he did not explain why the trade surplus dropped sharply in March.
Economists said Indonesia's economic fundamentals were fairly favourable compared with other countries in the region and they were not overly concerned about short-term volatility.
Some said the sharp drop in the trade surplus was due to softer oil prices in March. They expressed concern over possible increased consumer demand due to declining interest rates.

"In terms of oil exports, they have dropped 1.7 percent year-on-year. That was probably due to the lower oil prices for the month of March," Ng Bock Eng, economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Singapore, told Reuters.
"I think if you take a broader perspective rather than just month-to-month changes, it's still fairly relatively good numbers, compared to the region, for example," he said.
Exports in March were $4.06 billion while imports totalled $3.82 billion, with oil exports accounting for $960.9 million.

Harmoko said Indonesia's exports rose to $50.9 billion in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) from $46.5 billion in 1995/96. Imports were $43.9 billion, up from $41.3 billion. Oil and gas exports rose to $12.2 billion from $10.6 billion.
Indonesia posted a trade surplus of $6.98 billion in 1996/97 against $5.18 billion in 1995/96.

"The macro fundamentals are fairly favourable compared to the region. Some of these indicators are in fact improving, like inflation for example," Ng said, adding that interest rates were also falling, generating plenty of good signs for the Indonesian economy and the markets.
Ginanjar said the government was discussing a new economic deregulation package, including moves to cut import tariffs and boost the country's export competitiveness.
